From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Clean-Sheet: Pipeline Rules, Stage Mapping & Lab (May 12)

Team —

Following our last forecast sync, the finance and ops teams approved a tightened set of rules for how we classify deals into Pipeline / Best Case / Commit. The goal is a single source of truth so forecasts map to predictable ARR and we reduce the back-and-forth during close week.

Key changes (high level):
- Commit: deals with signed commercial terms (SLA on revenue recognition) OR an unequivocal verbal legal approval + agreed PO date.
- Best Case: deals with customer approval to proceed and an internal sales commitment, but awaiting final procurement/PO.
- Pipeline: all earlier-stage opportunities (discovery, evaluation, solutioning) without firm buy signals.

I attached a short PDF (pipeline_rules_v2.pdf) and a 45-minute "Clean-Sheet Lab" agenda (clean-sheet_lab_agenda.md). Please review before the session — the lab will be hands-on: each AE will open their top 10 deals and map them to the new rules.

Proposed lab: Tue, May 12, 11:00–11:45am PDT (calendar invite to follow).
Pre-work:
- Update HubSpot 'Forecast Category' and 'Forecast Reason' for your top 10 active deals (use the export template attached).
- Add one-line rationale in the 'Forecast Reason' for any Commit/Best Case entries.

Questions I want resolved in the lab:
- Consistent definition of Best Case across regions.
- Whether partner-sourced deals use a separate tag or inherit the same mapping.
- Expected rollback rules (e.g., when a Commit drops back to Best Case).

Please ACK and flag any conflicts for May 12. If anyone wants a separate slot for the APAC team, call it out here.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pipeline_rules_v2.pdf, clean-sheet_lab_agenda.md

Monica —

Thanks for running this. A couple quick clarifying items:

1) Best Case vs. Likely: are we aligning 'Best Case' to what we historically called 'Likely', or is there a behavior/acceptance criteria difference? Example: if AE has verbal exec sign-off but procurement is slow, is that Best Case or Commit per the new rules?

2) Region nuance: APAC procurement windows are different; can we add a region appendix rather than a single one-size-fits-all rule?

3) Partner-sourced deals: recommend a separate boolean 'partner_sourced' flag so we can roll up metrics without changing stage semantics.

I'll do the pre-work. One ask: can we add a short checklist for 'what constitutes a Commit' (e.g., signed SOW or signed email from procurement + date) so AEs use a consistent threshold?
